column1: # The shared b32_prefix conformance fixture.
# One vector set, three implementations: the POSIX-sh verifier in robot.sh
# (the CA pin check), the Rust minter in
# phases/03-ingest-server-rs/src/crockford.rs (the code's CA pin), and the Python
# encoder in packaging/robot-agent/agent/lib/ingotron_agent/crockford.py that
# `ingotron-agent status` uses to re-check the installed CA.
# This fixture is the main guard against a bug in the hand-written shell
# encoder: three implementations, one test-vector set. A drift between
# minter and verifier is a total enrollment outage.
# Columns, TAB-separated:  hex <TAB> want <TAB> expected_rc <TAB> expected_out
#   hex           the input; the literal token <empty> means the empty string
#                 (a leading empty field cannot survive a tab-separated read,
#                 because tab is IFS whitespace and leading IFS whitespace is
#                 stripped -- hence the sentinel)
#   expected_rc   0 = success, 1 = refusal
#   expected_out  "-" when expected_rc is 1; a refusal must emit NOTHING, since
#                 a partial answer would compare unequal and look like a MITM
# Rows 1-6 give the same result under dash, busybox ash and an independent
# Python encoder.
ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff
<empty>
abcd
zz
# Row 7 checks that the pin encodes 130 bits of the digest, and it is the only
# row that can catch a change to the wrong "encoding of SHA-256(SPKI)[0..16]" definition.
# 18 bytes: sixteen 0x00, then 0xff, then 0x00. Character 26 spans bit
# positions 125-129, so its low two bits come from byte 16 (0xff) and its value
# is 0b00011 = 3. Under the wrong definition only 16 bytes = 128 bits are
# available, which cannot produce 26 characters (130 bits) at all -- that
# definition zero-pads to get there. Verified against an independent Python
# encoder.
# Sub-26 widths: the same function is used for prefixes shorter than a pin.
